implementation_notes: A Scala case class generates structural `equals`/`hashCode`, `copy`, `toString` and `unapply` from its parameter list, and `==` forwards to `equals`, so instances compare by value everywhere - the classic hand-written value class plus manual equality and copying is replaced by one declaration. Case classes are shallow: only the constructor parameters participate, `copy` shares references, and deep immutability comes from the collections chosen (scala.collection.immutable); `AnyVal` value classes or opaque types cover the single-attribute case.
pitfalls: Equality is type-sensitive and parameter-based: adding a parameter changes equality and breaks the generated `copy`/`unapply` signatures for already-compiled clients.
A `var` parameter or a mutable collection member is only shallowly immutable - `copy` shares the collection between the old and the new value.
Extending a case class is discouraged: the generated equality does not consider subclass state, so model variants with a sealed hierarchy instead.
